=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3643 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The command `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true` swallows every `rev-parse` failure mode (missing directory, corrupt repository, permission error) into an empty string via `2>/dev/null || true`. The downstream `[[ "${review_source_sha}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]` check then fails, triggering `AUTOFIX_STALE_BASE_SKIP=true` with a single generic message that does not distinguish a genuine SHA mismatch from a broken checkout.
  WHY: The review is safely skipped either way (fail-safe direction), but a legitimately broken checkout such as a missing GITHUB_WORKSPACE or corrupt .git produces the same "Review source, workspace, and PR metadata heads differ" diagnostic as an actual SHA mismatch, slowing operator triage of an already-broken run.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38-39 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The exclusion `if name == "tests/test_audit_plans_command.py": return False` is an exact-match on one file path. If that test module is ever renamed, or a second operator-input-dependent test is added, the exclusion silently stops matching and the test re-enters the isolated-editor snapshot, where it fails at pytest-collection time with `FileNotFoundError` because the required `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` is intentionally outside the snapshot.
  WHY: The CI pipeline relies on this exclusion to keep the isolated editor testable; a rename would not break snapshot construction but would restore the collection failure from PR #6135 without any signal from the `allowed()` predicate itself. The failure is ultimately caught as a test failure, so the blast radius is contained, but the maintenance contract is fragile.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

If `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` is renamed, moved, or a second operator-input-dependent test is added (e.g. another test reading `.claude/commands/<x>.md` outside the isolation trust boundary), pytest collection in the isolated snapshot will trip the same `FileNotFoundError` mode this change exists to suppress — and the only diagnostic the isolation layer offers is the generic path-free `unsafe_directory` reason, so a future contributor has no signal from `allowed()` that the new test needed the same exemption.
  WHY: `allowed()` returns `False` only on literal `name == "tests/test_audit_plans_command.py"`. A renamed path passes through to the suffix allow-list, lands in the snapshot, and fails pytest at fixture-time exactly as PR #6135 did.

  WHY: A new operator-input test added today silently bypasses the trust boundary when the snapshot cannot supply its required input, with no audit trail linking the test to its exclusion.
